newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 10.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- More than 1,200 jobs are to be created in three new business ventures in counties Cork and Dublin.

- The Irish government is expected to resist pressure to sever links with senior officials of the IRA's political ally Sinn Fein during a special debate on Northern Ireland in the Irish parliament on Thursday.

- Almost 2.5 million Irish pounds is now believed to be missing after the disappearance of Dublin investment manager Tony Taylor, the Irish minister of state for Commerce, Science and Technology, Pat Rabbitte said on Wednesday.
- Pharmaceutical firm Sandoz is to increase its 250-strong workforce in County Cork by 100 in a 60-million-Irish-pound capital expansion.
- Sinn Fein and IRA leaders came under renewed attack on Wednesday as Irish prime minister John Bruton said their bomb-and-ballot strategy was comparable to the tactics of German Nazis.
- Irish motor cars of fours years and older will have to be tested for roadworthiness under a new governmnent scheme to be introduced in 1998.
- Irish private hospitals have differences of up to 2,500 Irish pounds in the cost of common operations, new healthcare figures revealed on Wednesday.
- Recruitment is to begin immediately to fill 400 financial services jobs in the investment group Fidelity's new Irish base at the International Financial Services Centre in Dublin.
- The Irish government has invited Irish business representive body ISME and 15 other organisations to participate in opening discussions for a new national pay agreement.
